source_statement.zero_convention: C(N,k)=0 for k<0 or k>N; guard middle term when j<i. The signed-binomial helper identities must preserve the same lower-index zero convention.
source_statement.faithful_complete_answer: For natural n, zero is an eigenvalue iff n>=1. At n=0, M_0=[3]. The full positive-n proof is required; n=0 alone is not counted as a disproof.
source_statement.field: Complex matrices faithfully express the ordinary eigenvalue question; integer/rational kernel and determinant arguments bridge to this characteristic-zero target.

mathematical_challenge.signed_identities: A and B follow from coefficient extraction in finite polynomial binomial expansions, C from (-X)^h. All uses have N>=h and valid zero-convention endpoints.
mathematical_challenge.odd_case: Lampe proposed nonzero left nullvector v_i=(-1)^i(C(n,i)+C(n+1,i)); its first coordinate2 is nonzero. Three summed components cancel exactly.
mathematical_challenge.even_case: MTyson proposed right nullvector w_j=(-1)^j C(2m-j,m)-2[j=m-1], m=n+1 odd>=3. Its first coordinate is positive; extending the raw sums adds only the j=m endpoint, and Pascal cancels the final terms.
mathematical_challenge.n0: The even-vector formula degenerates to zero at n=0 and is not used; M_0=[3] has no zero eigenvalue overC.
mathematical_challenge.finite_computation_role: Read the collaborator’s exact n1..60 screen receipt; it is corroboration only, not the universal proof and not claimed as independently rerun here.

papers.assessment: Results concern shifted symmetric Pascal minors, polynomial perturbations and fixed Pascal or diagonal recursions. No theorem supplying the exact M_n singularity for all positive n or a complete source-family specialization was located.

papers.name: Lunnon, The Pascal matrix (Fibonacci Quarterly15(3),1977,201–204)
papers.assessment: The symmetric matrix with entries C(i+j,i), its determinant1, inverse, positive minors and reciprocal eigenvalues are treated. That matrix is different from the three-term M_n; no exact source closure was located.
